info.title: Core System API
info.description: Enterprise Core System — capacités transverses (identity, ledger, wallet) exposées à plusieurs produits. Authentification par API key (`Authorization: Bearer pk_<env>_<id>.<secret>`), voir `GET /v1/whoami`.

get.description:
Resolves the bearer API key and returns which Project it belongs to,
in which environment (sandbox/live), and which scopes it carries. The
first call an integrating product should make to confirm its
credentials.

post.description:
Requires the `notifications:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key`
header (spec §13). `to_party_ref` is a correlation reference only
— resolving it to an actual delivery address is a provider adapter
concern, not the Core's (ADR-0041 §5).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-supplied unique key used for both the HTTP-level response cache and the use case's own duplicate-effect guard. Same key + same body = cached response, never a second effect. Same key + different body = 409. See ADR-0025 (idempotency design) and G7 (mandatory on every monetary mutation route).

post.description:
The request names only a `channel` (e.g. `mtn_momo`, `card`), never a
provider — `StartPaymentUseCase` resolves which adapter actually
handles it via the Project's routing configuration (ADR-0038 §2).
Requires the `payments:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header
(G7, ADR-0025). Crediting a wallet on success is never implicit — it
only happens if `wallet_recipient_external_ref` is given (ADR-0037).
Prefer `POST /v1/payments/paylink` or `POST /v1/payments/payin`
for new integrations.

get.description:
Reads the Core's own last-known state only — no live call to the
provider. Requires the `payments:read` scope, and returns the same
not-found response whether the payment doesn't exist or belongs to
another project.

idempotency_key.description:
Review finding, user-directed: this is the documented
fallback truth source when a webhook is missed — it must
hand back the same caller-supplied context the webhook
already does (its own Idempotency-Key, and the callback_url
it registered), or polling here loses information the
webhook has.

PaymentFlow.description: Discriminates between the two payment initiation flows exposed by aggregator-style providers. `Payin` is the synchronous, app-driven flow (used by mobile apps and server-to-server integrations that drive the customer through their own UX). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /payin`; CinetPay exposes it as `POST /v2/payment`; MTN exposes it as `POST /collection/.../requesttopay`.  `Paylink` is the hosted-link, redirect-driven flow (used by web apps that hand the customer off to a provider-hosted page). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /paylink`; CinetPay returns a `payment_url` alongside the same initiation call (the discriminator is implicit).  Providers that do not distinguish the two flows (e.g. CinetPay) treat `Payin` as the default and ignore the discriminator on the `InitiatePaymentCommand`.
PaymentFlow.title: PaymentFlow

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`. Authorization (the
`webhooks:write` scope) is checked in the controller against
`ProjectContext`, not here.

url.description:
`SafeOutboundUrlRule` (security review finding — this
used to accept any http(s) URL, including
internal/private targets: SSRF, and a persistent one at
that, since a registered endpoint is retried and
DLQ-replayed). Publicly reachable, no localhost, no
RFC1918 ranges, no link-local. Must be https in
production but http is accepted for local development.

events.description:
Event types this endpoint subscribes to. `*`
(single-element array) means "every event the Core
             * emits" — useful as a debugging crutch, avoid in
production (an endpoint subscribed to all events gets
every domain change). The currently-emitted event
types are listed in the enum on `events.*`; the Core
owns the event-type vocabulary, so adding a new event
type requires a Core release, not just a config change.

items.description: One event-type name per array element.

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.title: RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest

phone_number.description:
Phone number of the WhatsApp device that will display
the pairing code (E.164 preferred, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX`).
Forwarded to WAHA as the device identifier for the
linking flow. The Core never persists this — the
provider (WAHA) is the single source of truth for the
session state.

channel.description:
Channel the caller asks for — routed by
`ConfigNotificationProviderRouter`. The only channel
currently routed platform-wide is `whatsapp` (via WAHA,
ADR-0042).

to_party_ref.description:
Caller-supplied correlation reference for the recipient
— NOT a phone number, NOT an email address. Resolving it
to an actual delivery address is the provider adapter's
job (ADR-0041 §5). For WhatsApp via WAHA the adapter
reads the address from `variables.phone_number` (G4).

media_url.description:
Publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL of the file to send.
Must be `SafeOutboundUrlRule`-clean (no internal/private
targets, no SSRF). The adapter fetches it server-side
and re-hosts.

filename.description:
Filename to present to the recipient (e.g.
`invoice-1234.pdf`). Used for the attachment's display
name and content-disposition; the file's actual content
is fetched from `media_url`.

mimetype.description:
MIME type of the file (e.g. `application/pdf`,
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`).
Required because file extensions are not reliable
signals — the adapter uses this to set `Content-Type`
when re-uploading.

caption.description:
Optional caption rendered above the file in the
recipient's client (WhatsApp supports a short text +
file combo). UTF-8, no length cap at this layer.

variables.description:
Adapter-specific variables (e.g. `{phone_number}` for
WhatsApp). Shape is provider-defined; the Core forwards
the array as-is.

channel.description:
Channel the caller asks for — routed by
`ConfigNotificationProviderRouter` to whichever provider
chain is configured for this Project. The only channel
currently routed platform-wide is `whatsapp` (via WAHA,
ADR-0042); adding `sms`, `email`, etc. is a config +
adapter change, never an endpoint change.

to_party_ref.description:
Caller-supplied correlation reference for the recipient
— NOT a phone number, NOT an email address. Resolving it
to an actual delivery address is the provider adapter's
job (ADR-0041 §5). For WhatsApp via WAHA the adapter
reads the address from `variables.phone_number` (G4).

media_url.description:
Publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL of the image to send.
Must be `SafeOutboundUrlRule`-clean (no internal/private
targets, no SSRF — same rule as webhook endpoints). The
adapter fetches it server-side and re-hosts on the
provider; the caller does not upload binary.

filename.description:
Optional filename hint for the image (used by the
adapter when the provider forwards the media as a file
attachment).

mimetype.description:
Optional MIME type hint (e.g. `image/png`). When
omitted, the adapter infers from the URL extension or
the upstream `Content-Type`.

variables.description:
Adapter-specific variables (e.g.
`{phone_number, caption_locale}` for WhatsApp). Shape
is provider-defined; the Core forwards the array as-is.

channel.description:
Channel the caller asks for — routed by
`ConfigNotificationProviderRouter` to whichever provider
chain is configured for this Project. Mirrors
`Core\Notification\Contracts\NotificationChannel`: a
string value (not a closed enum) because the channel set
grows by config. The only channel currently routed
platform-wide is `whatsapp` (via WAHA, ADR-0042); adding
`sms`, `email`, etc. is a config + adapter change, never
an endpoint change.

to_party_ref.description:
Caller-supplied correlation reference for the recipient
— NOT a phone number, NOT an email address. Resolving it
to an actual delivery address is the provider adapter's
job (ADR-0041 §5). For WhatsApp via WAHA the adapter
reads the address from `variables.phone_number` (G4 —
never from `to_party_ref`). Typical value: a Project's
own user id, an order id, or any opaque token stable
per recipient.

text.description:
The message body — UTF-8, no length cap enforced here
(provider-specific limits apply downstream). Rendered
verbatim by the adapter; the Core does not interpolate
`variables` into it.
examples: Hello Marie, your order #1234 is confirmed.

variables.description:
Adapter-specific variables (e.g.
`{phone_number, template_id, locale}` for WhatsApp).
Shape is provider-defined; the Core forwards the array
as-is and never inspects it.

StartPaymentRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/payments`. Authorization (the `payments:write`
scope) is checked in the controller against `ProjectContext`, not
here — this class only validates shape, never identity.

No `idempotency_key` body field: the `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header
(required by the `idempotency` middleware ahead of this request ever
reaching validation — ADR-0025, G7) is the one value used for both
the HTTP-level response cache and `StartPaymentUseCase`'s own
provider-call protection. One key, not two.

`amount` is in minor units (e.g. cents) — never a decimal amount,
matching how it is stored (`bigint`, G5).

channel.description:
Channel the caller asks for — routed by
`ConfigPaymentProviderRouter` to whichever provider is
configured for this Project. Mirrors
`Core\Payment\Contracts\PaymentChannel`: a string value
(not a closed enum) because the channel set grows by
config, not by Core code change.

amount.description:
Amount in MINOR units (e.g. cents for USD/EUR, centimes
for XAF) — `bigint`, never a decimal (G5). The
decimal-to-minor conversion is the caller's
responsibility. `100000` here means 1000.00 in the
currency's major unit.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code. The provider
configured for `channel` must support it; otherwise the
request fails with 422 `unsupported-currency` before
reaching the wire.

reason.description:
Free-text label for the payment — shown to the customer
on the provider-hosted page (Paylink flow) and forwarded
to the provider as `description`. Not user-visible in the
API response.

customer_phone_number.description:
Customer phone number in international format
(E.164 preferred, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX`). Forwarded to the
provider so USSD / OTP prompts reach the right line for
mobile-money channels. May be required by some
providers — check the channel's adapter contract.

customer_name.description:
Customer display name — optional. Forwarded to the
provider where supported; rendered on the Paylink page
when present.

customer_email.description:
Customer email — optional. Forwarded to the provider for
receipt delivery where supported. Not used by the Core
itself (no PII persisted at this layer — ADR-0033 §4).

customer_lang.description:
BCP-47 language tag for the customer's locale (e.g.
`fr`, `en`, `fr-CM`). Forwarded to the provider so the
hosted page is rendered in the customer's language.

anyOf.description:
Discriminator between the two payment initiation flows
(ADR-0038). `payin` is the synchronous, app-driven flow
— caller drives the customer through their own UX.
`paylink` is the hosted-link, redirect-driven flow —
caller hands the customer off to a provider-hosted page.
When omitted, the provider default applies (typically
`payin`).

return_url.description:
Browser redirect URL after the customer completes (or
cancels) the payment on the provider-hosted page.
Best-effort: this is browser-side only, never a reliable
signal. For the reliable server-to-server notification,
use `callback_url` instead.

wallet_recipient_external_ref.description:
External reference of the wallet to credit on payment
success (ADR-0037). When present AND the payment reaches
a successful terminal state, the wallet is credited
synchronously in the same transaction (ADR-0036). When
absent, the payment is a pure collection — no wallet,
no Party touched. The value must match a wallet owned
by the calling Project (ADR-0051) or the call fails
with 422 `wallet-project-mismatch`.

callback_url.description:
The reliable server-to-server notification target —
SSRF validated the same way as POST /v1/webhook-endpoints
(security review finding, user-directed expansion,
ADR-0051). Delivered signed (HMAC-SHA256, secret
returned once at registration) per ADR-0009. Distinct
from `return_url` which is browser-side best-effort.
